messages.subject: New wiener distribution estimating parameters strangely from RWiener package
parts:
I'm trying to figure out why the parameters estimated when using the new wiener_log function differ quite dramatically from simulated data using the RWiener package. I generated some random response time values using the rwiener() function from the RWiener package, then tried to estimate the parameters from the simulated data in Stan. The Stan manual refers me to this R package so I assume the parameterization from the wiener distribution is the same in both Stan and RWiener. I'm uploading some example code for testing.

For example, simulated data from the RWiener package using parameters alpha = 3.25, tau = 0.25, beta = 0.4, delta = 0.65 will give me the following in Stan, 7.25, 0.22, 0.71, 0.93. This occurs even with a larger N and setting different priors on these four parameters. Any ideas?

EDIT: in case attachment isn't found

library(rstan)
library(loo)
library(RWiener)

# if running chains in parallel
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())

# wiener parameters
a <- 3.25
t <- 0.25
b <- 0.4
v <- 0.65
n <- 150

# random RT values from RWiener using parameters above
rt <- rwiener(
    n = n,
    alpha = a,
    tau = t,
    beta = b,
    delta = v
)

# make stan data list
stan_data <- list(rt = rt$q,
                  acc = ifelse(rt[, "resp"] == "upper", 1, 0),
                  n = nrow(rt))

# number of chains to run
n_chains <- 5

# use inits from above dist. parameters
stan_inits <- lapply(1:n_chains, function(i) {
    list(
        a_mu = max(c(0.0001, a)),
        t_mu = max(c(0.0001, t)),
        v_mu = max(c(0.0001, v)),
        a_raw = 0.01,
        t_raw = 0.01,
        v_raw = 0.01,
        a_sd = 1,
        t_sd = 1,
        v_sd = 1,
        b = b
    )
})

# STAN code
stan_model <-
"
data {
    int<lower=1>                n;
    vector[n]                   rt;
    vector<lower=0,upper=1>[n]  acc;
}
parameters {
    real<lower=0,upper=10> a_mu;
    real<lower=0,upper=3>  a_sd;
    real                   a_raw;
    real<lower=0,upper=3>  t_mu;
    real<lower=0,upper=2>  t_sd;
    real                   t_raw;
    real<lower=0,upper=5>  v_mu;
    real<lower=0,upper=2>  v_sd;
    real                   v_raw;
    real<lower=0,upper=1>  b;     // <- beta
}
transformed parameters {
    real a; // <- alpha
    real t; // <- tau
    real v; // <- delta

    a <- a_mu + a_sd * a_raw; // a ~ normal(a_mu, a_sd)
    t <- t_mu + t_sd * t_raw; // t ~ normal(t_mu, t_sd)
    v <- v_mu + v_sd * v_raw; // v ~ normal(v_mu, v_sd)
}
model {
    a_raw ~ normal(0,1);
    t_raw ~ normal(0,1);
    v_raw ~ normal(0,1);
    b ~ beta(2, 2);

    // likelihood
    for (i in 1:n) {
        if (acc[n] == 1) {
            rt[i] ~ wiener(a, t, b, v);    // upper bound
        } else {
            rt[i] ~ wiener(a, t, 1-b, -v); // lower bound
        }
    }
}
generated quantities {
    vector[n] log_lik;

    for (i in 1:n) {
        if (acc[n] == 1) { // upper
            log_lik[i] <- wiener_log(rt[i], a, t, b, v);
        } else { // lower
            log_lik[i] <- wiener_log(rt[i], a, t, 1-b, -v);
        }
    }
}
"

# run model
stan_fit <-
    stan(
        model_name = "diffusion_test",
        model_code = stan_model,
        data = stan_data,
        init = stan_inits,
        chains = n_chains
    )

# print stan model parameters
print(stan_fit)

# print elpd_loo
print(loo(extract_log_lik(stan_fit)), digits = 3)

# print RWiener likelihood
print(wiener_likelihood(c(a,t,b,v), rt))


# Plots -------------------------------------------------------------------

# stan traceplot
traceplot(stan_fit)

# plot distributions from RWiener
plot_rwiener <- function(rt) {
    rt_u <- rt$q[rt$resp == "upper"]
    rt_l <- rt$q[rt$resp == "lower"]

    xlim <- max(c(rt_u, rt_l))
    rt_seq <- seq(0, xlim, .005)

    d_rt_u <-
        dwiener(rt_seq, a, t, b, v, resp = rep("upper", length(rt_seq)))
    d_rt_l <-
        dwiener(rt_seq, a, t, b, v, resp = rep("lower", length(rt_seq)))

    ylim <- max(c(d_rt_u, d_rt_l))

    par(mfrow = c(3, 1))

    plot(
        x = rt_seq,
        y = d_rt_u,
        type = "l",
        xlim = c(0, xlim),
        ylim = c(-ylim, ylim),
        main = "Density of upper/lower responses",
        ylab = "density",
        xlab = "quantile",
        col = "green"
    )

    lines(x = rt_seq, y = -d_rt_l, col = "red")

    xbrks <- seq(0, xlim, length.out = 30)

    hist(
        rt_u,
        freq = FALSE,
        breaks = xbrks,
        xlim = c(0, xlim),
        ylim = c(0, ylim * 2),
        main = "upper",
        xlab = paste("N =", length(rt_u))
    )

    hist(
        rt_l,
        freq = FALSE,
        breaks = xbrks,
        xlim = c(0, xlim),
        ylim = c(0, ylim * 2),
        main = "lower",
        xlab = paste("N =", length(rt_l))
    )
}

plot_rwiener(rt)

parts:
is there a specific reason you don't simply specify a prior for a (and v and t)?*
it looks as if your statistical model is more complex than the true generative model.
i.e. when you generate the data 
a <- 3.25 
but in your stan model 
a <- a_mu + a_sd * a_raw.

so  I think 
a ~ normal(0,2);
after specifying real<lower=0,upper=10> a; 
in the parameters block and removing a_mu, a_raw, and a_sd should work better.
(same for v and t).

maybe you can try this simpler model first
(I had no issues to recover the correct wiener parameter values 
when testing such a simple model a few weeks ago).

personally, I would try this simpler model first and see if I can recover parameters, 
before trying the more complex model. but if you do this and you use
a <- a_mu + a_sd * a_raw;

in stan, then you might also want to generate the data in R accordingly

I also would use more informative priors than the (implicit) flat priors you used for 
a_mu, a_sd, ... you have in your model.

guido

*(maybe this is a preparation to run the full DDM with between trial variability for v,a,t?)

    n = n,
    alpha = a,
    tau = t,
    beta = b,
    delta = v
)

                  acc = ifelse(rt[, "resp"] == "upper", 1, 0),
                  n = nrow(rt))

# use inits from above dist. parameters
stan_inits <- lapply(1:n_chains, function(i) {
    list(
        a_mu = max(c(0.0001, a)),
        t_mu = max(c(0.0001, t)),
        v_mu = max(c(0.0001, v)),
        a_raw = 0.01,
        t_raw = 0.01,
        v_raw = 0.01,
        a_sd = 1,
        t_sd = 1,
        v_sd = 1,
        b = b
    )

"

    int<lower=1>                n;
    vector[n]                   rt;
    vector<lower=0,upper=1>[n]  acc;

    real<lower=0,upper=10> a_mu;
    real<lower=0,upper=3>  a_sd;
    real                   a_raw;
    real<lower=0,upper=3>  t_mu;
    real<lower=0,upper=2>  t_sd;
    real                   t_raw;
    real<lower=0,upper=5>  v_mu;
    real<lower=0,upper=2>  v_sd;
    real                   v_raw;
    real<lower=0,upper=1>  b;     // <- beta
}
transformed parameters {
    real a; // <- alpha
    real t; // <- tau
    real v; // <- delta

    a <- a_mu + a_sd * a_raw; // a ~ normal(a_mu, a_sd)
    t <- t_mu + t_sd * t_raw; // t ~ normal(t_mu, t_sd)
    v <- v_mu + v_sd * v_raw; // v ~ normal(v_mu, v_sd)

    t_raw ~ normal(0,1);
    v_raw ~ normal(0,1);

        } else {

        }
    }

            log_lik[i] <- wiener_log(rt[i], a, t, b, v);
        } else { // lower
            log_lik[i] <- wiener_log(rt[i], a, t, 1-b, -v);
        }
    }

        ylab = "density",
        xlab = "quantile",
        col = "green"
    )

        rt_u,
        freq = FALSE,
        breaks = xbrks,
        xlim = c(0, xlim),
        ylim = c(0, ylim * 2),

        xlab = paste("N =", length(rt_u))
    )

        freq = FALSE,
        breaks = xbrks,
        xlim = c(0, xlim),
        ylim = c(0, ylim * 2),
        main = "lower",
        xlab = paste("N =", length(rt_l))
    )
}
